subject: A round pavilion roof surveyed from directly above: its tile courses are concentric orbits round the ridge finial, one course per note of the span, and each drop that lands sits on its course like a planet, with the gutter as the outermost orbit where the puddle's held notes circle.
controls: rate: how many drop marks sit on the courses from the last bar (count): one or two at 0.25 a beat, about thirty at 8 a beat, newest brightest and older ones fading to hollow rings.
roof: how many concentric course rings the plan holds between finial and eave (count, plus ring spacing as position): one ring at 0 st, eight at 12, twenty-two at 36 crowding toward the 3 px floor.
gust: every drop mark slides round its orbit in the wind's direction (rotation about the finial, up to ±90° at full gust), with a bearing arc outside the gutter showing which way and how far.
puddle: beads collect on the gutter orbit, one per repeated note, joined by a link drawn along the gutter in the direction they replay (count): none at 0, a near-full ring at 100.
reference: library/meikyu-orrery/README.md (concentric orbits round a body, built in 3D and projected; here the projection is straight down)
risks: A plan view throws away the depth that makes meikyu's orrery read as a solar system; at 1:1 it can read as a target, which craft.md names as an icon to avoid. The hips and survey labels are what stop it, and they're hairlines.
Rings are 10 px apart at 12 st but 3 px at 36 st; the roof control has to cap the drawn rings (one per scale octave degree, not per semitone) or it turns to hatching.
Gust and puddle are both empty at their defaults (0 and 0), so the rest frame shows neither; gust's rotation of the drops only reads once there are drops.
Orbits suggest a cycle, but rain isn't periodic; only puddle (the replay loop) is truly a cycle. The metaphor fits one control in four.
Muted state: the drops would have to go hollow and the finial dark; not yet drawn.
